transcript:
Meeting: Lynx Medical postmortem and hardening handoff
Date: 2026-11-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Sana Patel (Head of Platform), Dr. Ravi Kapoor (CTO), Janel Morales (SRE Lead), Marcus Lee (Security)

Summary section (auto):
- Brief timeline recap of 2026-11-03 02:14UTC degradation incident
- Root cause hypothesis: KV cache thrash + aggressive scale-down causing cold starts and tail latency surge
- Short-term mitigations discussed: increase cache TTLs, adjust autoscaler cooldowns, introduce circuit-breaker for model variant fallback

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the root cause we traced for the degrada- degradation early this week and make sure the hardening runbook covers the ops steps you need.
[00:00:14] Sana Patel: thanks, Maya. biggest thing for us is we can't have that latency spike during our clinical ingestion window, it's patient facing if it delays notes.
[00:00:22] Luis Ortega: absolutely. quick show of hands, who has the timeline open? i'll start with the TL;DR then Ravi can add details.
[00:00:30] Dr. Ravi Kapoor: i've got it. from SRE side we saw a two-phase pattern: a traffic burst at 02:13, followed by node preemptions and an autoscaler shrink at 02:16, then KV cache misses spiked and token latencies ballooned.
[00:00:50] Janel Morales: to add, the initial KV cache evictions looked correlated with a background job that runs every hour, which coincided with a tail of requests from a downstream partner. so combo effect.
[00:01:02] Priya Nair: (muted) quick note - we logged the alerts and attached the slow traces in the drive link.
[00:01:10] Maya Chen: perfect. so root cause we believe is interaction of cache TTL/eviction policy and the autoscaler's cooldown and preemption on spot type instances, which created repeated cold KV loads. that increased token counts and cpu on the inference runtime, pushing other requests to the slow path.
[00:01:34] Marcus Lee: on the security side we flagged that the audit logs during that window were truncated — not a compliance failure yet, but it's close and we need to ensure retention and immutability for SOC 2 scope.
[00:01:50] Luis Ortega: yeah on the runtime side there were two compounding things: the KV (k-v) cache impl has an LRU threshold that when combined with concurrent prefix caching results in churning; and the autoscaler was configured to scale down aggressively at low average CPU but didn't account for percentiles, so we had insufficient warm workers.
[00:02:20] Sana Patel: is this specific to the model variant you were running? we had pinned a slightly higher-capacity variant for accuracy last month. could that have changed memory footprint?
[00:02:33] Luis Ortega: it might — the larger variant keeps larger kv shards in memory, which actually increases eviction pressure when instances are tight. our profiling shows ~18% more KV resident memory on the variant you pinned.
[00:02:50] Dr. Ravi Kapoor: can we short-term rollback to the smaller variant? we prefer predictable latency over marginal accuracy improvements for now.
[00:03:00] Maya Chen: that is an option; we recommended a canary to validate accuracy regression. but immediate action is to change cache TTL and autoscaler cooldown so we don't see that thrash.
[00:03:15] Janel Morales: for the runbook we need exact commands and thresholds - e.g., set TTL to 30m, autoscaler cooldown to 300s, and set min replicas to 4 during the clinical window.
[00:03:28] Luis Ortega: noted. we can propose those exact numbers in the runbook. also introduce a circuit breaker rule: if 95th token latency > 1200ms for 5m, fallback to smaller variant or to a reduced token budget.
[00:03:46] Marcus Lee: from security we also need a KMS attestation for the fallback variant so keys aren't re-initialized mid-flight, and a note about HSM-backed keys for the private deployment.
[00:03:58] Maya Chen: ok adding that. quick audience question — do you prefer us to handle runbook changes via your SRE repo (CI) or send a runbook we can apply together during the canary?
[00:04:10] Sana Patel: we'd like a draft to import into our repo, then schedule a joint apply during canary window. helps with audit history.
[00:04:19] Priya Nair: i'll coordinate the import.
[00:04:23] Luis Ortega: one subtlety — there was also some sustained small requests that filled KV keyspace from a long-tail process, probably a telemetry batch. it's low rps but lots of unique prefixes, which is worst-case for prefix caching.
[00:04:40] Janel Morales: that telemetry job we can throttle or move to off-peak; i'll take that back.
[00:04:46] Dr. Ravi Kapoor: we also ran into a problem where the monitoring dashboards didn't alert on the right percentile; dashboards showed median fine which masked the tail.
[00:04:56] Maya Chen: we'll add a dashboard template for 90/95/99th token latency and queue depth. Luis, you'll send the Grafana panel?
[00:05:05] Luis Ortega: yes i will.
[00:05:08] [00:05:08] Speaker 6: (background) yep, thanks.
[00:05:15] Maya Chen: moving into mitigation categories: immediate (hotfix during working hours), short-term (canary + runbook), and longer-term (metrics, autoscaler improvements, runtime optimizations).
[00:05:28] Sana Patel: can you be specific on hotfix? we need exact steps we can execute if this happens again tonight.
[00:05:35] Luis Ortega: hotfix is 4 steps: 1) increase cache TTL from 5m to 30m, 2) set min replicas to 4, 3) bump autoscaler cooldown to 300s, 4) enable circuit breaker fallback to smaller variant. these can be rolled back within 2 minutes.
[00:05:52] Janel Morales: what's the rollback risk on the KV cache change? any data corruption?
[00:05:58] Luis Ortega: no data corruption, only cache miss rate will change; the runtime is safe.
[00:06:05] Marcus Lee: is there any credential rotation implicit? if we change variants we need to ensure keys are pre-loaded so key material isn't fetched live.
[00:06:14] Luis Ortega: good point — pre-warming HSM/KMS connections is in the runbook. we'll add a checklist to validate key availability.
[00:06:24] [00:06:24] Maya Chen: ok. next, telemetry and observability - we recommend adding an alert on token queue depth and a separate alert for a sudden increase in KV miss rate above 20% sustained for 3m.
[00:06:38] Sana Patel: can that alert be routed to our pager and to Redwood's SRE on-call? it's critical.
[00:06:45] Priya Nair: yes we can set up joint paging for the canary period.
[00:06:50] Luis Ortega: also, we suggest adding a lightweight replay harness that replays a subset of recent requests to validate accuracy of smaller variant before automated fallback.
[00:07:00] Dr. Ravi Kapoor: that's useful. will you provide the harness?
[00:07:03] Luis Ortega: we'll provide a script and sample dataset.
[00:07:08] [00:07:08] Speaker 1: (paper rustle)
[00:07:12] Janel Morales: on the longer-term side, we should address autoscaler logic — use percentile CPU and token queue metrics for scale decisions rather than average, and consider buffer replicas for spot preemption windows.
[00:07:26] Luis Ortega: adding to that, we can recommend using dedicated instances for critical windows (dedicated pool) if predictability is more important than cost.
[00:07:35] Sana Patel: that's a cost conversation we'll need to run internally. can you provide estimated cost delta for reserving a small dedicated pool for 6 hours/day?
[00:07:44] Maya Chen: yes, Luis will include cost delta in the perf spreadsheet.
[00:07:49] Marcus Lee: security follow-ups: we need proof of audit log retention and an SOP for log export to our SIEM. also a KMS rotation schedule for the next quarter.
[00:07:59] Priya Nair: i'll include the SOC 2 artifacts and the KMS guide in the share.
[00:08:04] [00:08:04] Maya Chen: great. moving toward runbook handoff - we'll prepare a trimmed runbook with the hotfix commands, canary plan, monitoring panels, and a checklist for security pre-reqs.
[00:08:17] Luis Ortega: and i'll add a troubleshooting checklist for KV churning: commands to inspect cache hit ratios, identify top prefixes, and sample traces for a long-tail key load.
[00:08:29] Janel Morales: would love a one-line play to reduce tail while we investigate: something reversible and low-risk.
[00:08:36] Luis Ortega: the single-line play is 'scale-up min replicas to 4 and set TTL 30m' which we can execute via your infra tool.
[00:08:44] Sana Patel: okay. schedule wise, we want the canary before our validation window begins on 11/18.
[00:08:51] Maya Chen: proposed canary 11/18 to 11/20. follow-up sync 11/17 to review pre-canary checks.
[00:08:59] [00:08:59] (crosstalk)
[00:09:05] Marcus Lee: one more compliance question: during the incident we saw truncated audit logs; is that due to retention tiering on your side or a push failure?
[00:09:14] Luis Ortega: preliminary is a push failure — our log shipper retried but some chunks were lost during node preemption. we'll propose a push-retry backoff change and local buffering for critical audit events.
[00:09:28] Maya Chen: action item for Marcus: confirm retention policy and we will align shipper settings.
[00:09:35] Marcus Lee: noted.
[00:09:37] [00:09:37] Maya Chen: okay let's do a quick readout of action items so nothing is missed.
[00:09:42] Janel Morales: Janel - throttle telemetry job to off-peak and share findings (due 11/16).
[00:09:49] Luis Ortega: Luis - send perf spreadsheet + Grafana panels + replay harness (due 11/12).
[00:09:55] Maya Chen: Maya - runbook draft and canary plan (due 11/13).
[00:09:59] Marcus Lee: Marcus - KMS attestation and confirm audit retention (due 11/20).
[00:10:05] Dr. Ravi Kapoor: Ravi - internal decision on variant rollback if canary fails (due 11/17).
[00:10:12] Sana Patel: Sana - schedule canary window and grant Redwood limited access to your staging infra during the test (due 11/15).
[00:10:20] Priya Nair: and I'll upload SOC2 docs and the security checklist to the drive now.
[00:10:24] [00:10:24] (short pause)
[00:10:28] Maya Chen: quick technical question from me - during the incident, were there any unusual request patterns we should know about?
[00:10:33] Janel Morales: yes a few thousand low-weight requests with unique prefixes from a partner ingestion stream; looked like a retry storm.
[00:10:40] Luis Ortega: that retry storm exacerbated prefix variety which is expensive for prefix/kv cache. we'll add a rate-limit recommendation for partners.
[00:10:49] Dr. Ravi Kapoor: is Redwood able to throttle at the network ingress level per client?
[00:10:55] Luis Ortega: yes we can apply per-client rate limits and also offer token budget limiting per API key.
[00:11:03] Maya Chen: we'll add those to the runbook as optional mitigations.
[00:11:09] [00:11:09] Speaker 2: (agrees)
[00:11:15] Luis Ortega: operational note — for private deployments we can pre-provision KMS keys and HSM-backed instances to avoid runtime fetching; for hosted we have a KMS handshake that we can pre-warm during canary.
[00:11:29] Marcus Lee: please include HSM checklist; the compliance team will expect it.
[00:11:35] Maya Chen: will do. any other concerns?
[00:11:39] Sana Patel: just want clarity on rollback criteria during canary - if 95th latency increases by > 10% over baseline and error rate > 0.5% we stop.
[00:11:50] Luis Ortega: agreed, we'll codify those metrics in the canary plan.
[00:11:56] Maya Chen: great. final reminder: we'll send the runbook, perf sheet, and dashboard panels by 11/13. follow-up sync 11/17 at 16:00 UTC. canary 11/18-11/20.
[00:12:10] Janel Morales: thanks everyone.
[00:12:13] Dr. Ravi Kapoor: thanks.
[00:12:15] (meeting ends)

Post-call notes (auto):
- Links: runbook draft (pending), perf spreadsheet (pending), Grafana panels (pending), SOC2 package (drive link provided by Priya)
- Risks: if long-tail prefix growth isn't contained, repeated tail spikes possible; dedicated pool recommended if cost acceptable.
